attempted_claim: Let (M^n,g(t))_{t in [-T,0)}, n>=3, be a Ricci flow on a closed manifold developing a finite-time singularity at t=0, and let (p,0) be a singular point with Bamler/Perelman tangent flows defined by parabolic rescalings with (singular) conjugate-heat-kernel basepoint. Suppose one tangent flow at (p,0) is, as a gradient shrinker, isometric (up to diffeomorphism and the standard normalisation) to the smooth complete U(n)-invariant shrinking gradient Kahler-Ricci soliton X^{n,1} on O(-1) -> CP^{n-1} constructed by Feldman-Ilmanen-Knopf (the case k=1, 0<k<n), which is asymptotically conical at infinity. Prove that every tangent flow at (p,0) is then isometric to the same FIK shrinker X^{n,1}.
decisive_failure: The investigation was limited to analytic routes available for the noncompact asymptotically conical FIK shrinker: entropy isolation, Lojasiewicz-Simon integrability, and Bamler cone rigidity. No spectral theory of the shrinker operator on AC ends, no singular-soliton classification, and no new computations beyond the diagnostic symmetric ODE reduction were established.
